providers.service_territory: Most of Wyoming (largest IOU in state; serves central, western, and southern Wyoming including Casper, Laramie, Lander, Green River, Rock Springs, Evanston, Sheridan)
providers.notes: Dominant IOU; serves most of WY. Operates under P.S.C. Wyoming No. 19 tariff. Wattsmart Business program updated October 24, 2025. Rate increase case (Docket 20000-710-ER-26) pending as of 2026.

providers.provider_name: Cheyenne Light, Fuel and Power (d/b/a Black Hills Energy)
providers.service_territory: Cheyenne metro area and surrounding Laramie County, Wyoming
providers.notes: IOU subsidiary of Black Hills Corp.; serves ~45,390 electric customers in Cheyenne area. DSM rebate programs suspended Jan 1, 2026 pending PSC approval of new DSM plan (Docket 20003-259-EA-25). Previously offered commercial electric rebates through Dec 31, 2025.

providers.provider_name: Black Hills Power (d/b/a Black Hills Energy)
providers.service_territory: Northeast Wyoming including Gillette, Newcastle, Sundance, Weston County
providers.notes: IOU serving northeast Wyoming (Weston County). Commercial electric rebate program discontinued; Weston County no longer accepting applications. General rate increase case pending (PSC Docket noted on Hot Topics page). Separate entity from CLFP but same Black Hills Energy brand.

providers.service_territory: Northwest Wyoming (Jackson Hole, Teton County, Star Valley) and southeast Idaho
providers.notes: Consumer-owned electric cooperative. Offers commercial lighting rebates based on kWh savings. Rates effective April 29, 2026. Wholesale supply primarily from Bonneville Power Administration (hydropower). 7.9% average retail rate increase effective October 2025 due to BPA increases.

providers.service_territory: Northeast Wyoming (Sheridan, Buffalo, Gillette portions, Campbell County)
providers.notes: IOU serving northeast Wyoming. Historically offered energy efficiency lighting incentive payments for commercial/industrial customers per EERE documentation. Current commercial electric rebate program status in WY unconfirmed as of 2025-2026; primary rebate effort appears to be gas-side. Included as a documented WY IOU per PSC and industry sources.

programs.program_notes_ai: Covers lighting, HVAC, compressed air, motors, and other equipment upgrades. Program updated October 24, 2025 with adjustments to lighting and green motor rewind offerings. Eligible rate schedules for oil/gas customers include Schedules 25, 28, 33, 40, 46, 48T, 54, 58, 210, 212, and 213. Incentive check issued within 45 days of final inspection/documentation receipt. DLC listed luminaires required for lighting fixtures. IECC 2009 used as baseline for new construction.

programs.program_name: Wattsmart Business – Small and Medium Business Express (2025)
required_documents: Trade ally invoice showing incentive credit
programs.stacking_rules: Available only through participating Small and Medium Business Express trade allies; incentive applied as invoice credit not check
programs.rebate_payment_method: Vendor Credit (Rocky Mountain Power pays up to 75% of project materials and installation directly to the vendor; customer does not receive a check)
programs.program_notes_ai: Formerly called Small Business Enhanced; renamed and expanded to include medium customers effective October 24, 2025. Focuses on LED lighting upgrades and lighting controls. Customer eligibility based on consolidated kW/kWh usage data (not rate schedule). Must use a participating Express Trade Ally. Incentive appears as credit on customer invoice. Rocky Mountain Power pays vendor directly up to 75% of project cost.

programs.program_name: Wattsmart Business – Custom / Large Business Incentives (2025)
programs.program_notes_ai: Provides technical assistance and cash incentives for large commercial and industrial customers. Custom projects require energy expert evaluation before purchase. Team assists in evaluating technology solutions and estimating savings. Energy management (no/low-cost system optimization) and capital custom projects both available. Pre-approval required; pre-inspection establishes energy baseline before equipment removal/purchase.

required_documents: Online application or signed General Application
programs.stacking_rules: New construction and major renovation must receive pre-approval; projects completed prior to pre-authorization are not eligible
programs.program_notes_ai: Pre-approval required before project completion; projects completed without pre-authorization are ineligible. Uses IECC 2009 as energy code baseline. As of October 2025 updates, whole-building incentives distinguish between all-electric HVAC vs. other HVAC systems and added a new Green Building Certification offering. LED fixtures must be DLC or ENERGY STAR listed.

programs.program_name: Wattsmart Business – Oil and Gas Incentives (2025)
required_documents: Proof of Rocky Mountain Power service (if in field areas near other providers)
programs.program_notes_ai: Tailored for production, transportation, and refining sectors. Program provides funded engineering services to identify energy savings opportunities. Two project types: energy management (no/low-cost system optimization) and custom capital projects. Eligible customers must be on rate schedules 25, 28, 33, 40, 46, 48T, 54, 58, 210, 212, or 213. Pre-inspection required to establish baseline before any equipment removal. Cash incentive paid within 45 days of final inspection and documentation.

programs.program_name: Wattsmart Business – Lighting Midstream / Distributor Program (2025)
programs.stacking_rules: Incentive flows to distributor, not end customer; complementary to customer-facing prescriptive programs
programs.program_notes_ai: Incentives paid directly to distributors who promote and stock high-efficiency LED lighting for Rocky Mountain Power Wyoming commercial customers. As of October 2025 updates, market incentives were shifted to distributors to better influence stocking practices. End customers do not apply directly; savings realized through lower product pricing at point of sale.

programs.program_name: Wattsmart Business – Agricultural / Farm and Dairy (2025)
programs.program_notes_ai: Targets farms and dairies for efficiency improvements. Covers pumping systems, lighting, refrigeration, and other agricultural equipment. Emphasis on high-energy-intensive pumps per DSM plan documentation. Cash incentives help bridge economic gap to reduce operational costs.

programs.provider_name: Cheyenne Light, Fuel and Power (d/b/a Black Hills Energy)
programs.program_name: Commercial and Industrial Demand Side Management (DSM) Electric Rebate Program (2025)
programs.program_notes_ai: CLFP (Black Hills Energy) electric commercial DSM rebate program was authorized through December 31, 2025. All rebate programs suspended as of January 1, 2026 until further notice. CLFP filed proposed new DSM plan with Wyoming PSC on July 1, 2025 (Docket No. 20003-259-EA-25, Record No. 17884) and is awaiting Commission decision before reopening. Applications were accepted through January 31, 2026 for equipment installed Jan 1–Dec 31, 2025. DSM rider charge continues to appear on customer bills (Sheet No. 45 of tariff). Covered measures historically included lighting, HVAC, motors, and other C&I equipment.

Lower Valley Energy (consumer-owned co-op) offers commercial rebates for lighting measures; rebate amounts vary based on kWh savings. Also offers residential energy efficiency rebates. Rates and programs effective April 29, 2026 following a 7.9% average retail rate increase in October 2025 driven by BPA wholesale increases. Visit program website for current incentive details.

rate_schedules.description: General service for small commercial customers without demand metering; served under P.S.C. Wyoming No. 19
rate_schedules.notes: Approximate base rates from Price Summary effective June 1, 2025 per Docket 20000-671-ER-24. Subject to ECAM (Schedule 95), Schedule 93 REC/SO2, Schedule 191 Customer Efficiency Service Charge, and Schedule 198 Carbon Capture Surcharge riders. Exact per-kWh values should be confirmed in the full tariff PDF.

rate_schedules.description: Optional TOU variant of Schedule 6 for small commercial; on-peak hours 7–9 a.m. and 4–11 p.m. all days
rate_schedules.notes: On-peak/off-peak hours per Price Summary: on-peak 7 a.m.–9 a.m. and 4 p.m.–11 p.m. all days; off-peak all remaining hours. Approximate rates; subject to all applicable riders. Confirm in full tariff.

rate_schedules.description: Demand-metered service for commercial customers at secondary voltage; typically 25–1,000 kW
rate_schedules.notes: Approximate base rates per Price Summary effective June 1, 2025 (Docket 20000-671-ER-24). Subject to ECAM and other riders. Confirm exact values in full P.S.C. Wyoming No. 19 tariff. Referenced in Wattsmart Small & Medium Business Express eligibility criteria.

rate_schedules.description: Primary voltage service for large commercial and industrial customers; typically 1,000+ kW or primary metering
rate_schedules.notes: Approximate base rates from Price Summary effective June 1, 2025. One of the eligible rate schedules for Oil & Gas Wattsmart Business incentives. Subject to all applicable riders. Confirm in full tariff.

rate_schedules.description: Time-of-use demand schedule at secondary voltage; on-peak 7–9 a.m. and 4–11 p.m. all days
rate_schedules.notes: Approximate rates per Price Summary. Listed as eligible rate schedule for Oil & Gas Wattsmart program. On-peak/off-peak periods: 7 a.m.–9 a.m. and 4 p.m.–11 p.m. all days; off-peak all remaining hours per Price Summary. Subject to riders.

rate_schedules.description: Seasonal irrigation and agricultural pumping service; listed in P.S.C. Wyoming No. 19
rate_schedules.notes: Listed as an eligible rate schedule for Wattsmart Oil & Gas (Schedule 46 cited in oil/gas eligibility list). Approximate rates; confirm in full tariff. Subject to applicable riders.

rate_schedules.description: Transmission-voltage service for very large industrial customers; eligible for Wattsmart Oil & Gas program
rate_schedules.notes: Listed among eligible rate schedules for Oil & Gas Wattsmart Business incentives (Schedules 25, 28, 33, 40, 46, 48T, 54, 58, 210, 212, 213). Approximate rates; confirm in full P.S.C. Wyoming No. 19 tariff. Subject to riders.

rate_schedules.description: Street and area lighting service; Schedule 95 ECAM rates also apply to Schedule 51 customer-funded conversion lamps
rate_schedules.notes: Per-fixture pricing structure. Schedule 95 ECAM rider applies to Schedule 51 customer-funded conversion lamps per tariff documentation. Confirm exact fixture rates in full tariff.

rate_schedules.provider_name: Cheyenne Light, Fuel and Power (d/b/a Black Hills Energy)
rate_schedules.description: Small commercial service under 25 kW demand; no demand metering
rate_schedules.notes: Approximate rates for CLFP (Black Hills Energy Wyoming - Cheyenne). Per Nectar research, CLFP commercial customers fall into three classes: Commercial Service (under 25 kW), Secondary General Service (demand-metered secondary voltage), and Primary General Service. Subject to DSM rider (Sheet No. 45), BCCA rider (Sheets 35–36), and Carbon Capture Compliance Surcharge. Confirm exact values in current CLFP tariff on file with Wyoming PSC.

rate_schedules.provider_name: Cheyenne Light, Fuel and Power (d/b/a Black Hills Energy)
rate_schedules.description: Demand-metered service at secondary voltage for medium commercial customers; 25 kW and above
rate_schedules.notes: Approximate rates. Subject to DSM rider (Sheet No. 45), BCCA rider, Carbon Capture Compliance Surcharge, and Power Cost Adjustment (PCA). PCA increase of $0.00481/kWh applied per Docket 20003-271-EM-26 (May 2026). Confirm in current CLFP tariff.

rate_schedules.provider_name: Cheyenne Light, Fuel and Power (d/b/a Black Hills Energy)
rate_schedules.description: Primary voltage service for large commercial and industrial customers in Cheyenne area
rate_schedules.notes: Approximate rates. Subject to DSM rider, BCCA rider, Carbon Capture Compliance Surcharge, and PCA riders. Confirm exact values in CLFP tariff on file with Wyoming PSC (Docket 20003-259-EA-25 for DSM).

rate_schedules.description: Small commercial service under 10 kW connected demand; hydropower-heavy supply from BPA
rate_schedules.notes: Rates effective April 29, 2026 following 7.9% average increase effective October 2025. Facility (base) charges tier by service size. Small commercial rate ~6.6¢/kWh per Nectar analysis. Consumer-owned cooperative; no retail choice in territory.

rate_schedules.schedule_name: Large Commercial Service (10 kW and above)
rate_schedules.description: Large commercial service with demand metering; approximately 4.34¢/kWh energy plus $7.70/kW demand charge
rate_schedules.notes: Rates effective April 29, 2026. Facility charges tier by service size (under 10 kW, 10–15 kW, over 15 kW). Board planning residential demand charges in late 2026 with offsetting energy-charge reductions; commercial demand structure already in place. Confirm exact customer charge on LVE rates page.

forms.form_notes: Primary application form for all Wattsmart Business prescriptive projects in Wyoming. Must be signed and submitted along with IRS Form W-9. Online submission also available at WattsmartBusiness.com.
Required for all Wattsmart Business incentive payments to allow preparation of 1099-MISC if required. Must accompany General Application or online application submission.

forms.form_name: Wattsmart Business HVAC Incentive Application – Wyoming
forms.form_notes: HVAC-specific application supplement for Wyoming Wattsmart Business prescriptive program. Includes participant business name (must match W-9), facility owner/tenant status, and optional incentive assignment section. Incentive check issued to participant business name/address unless assignment section completed.

Lighting-specific incentive catalog and post-purchase application for Wyoming; effective October 24, 2025. Includes prescriptive incentive tables, DLC/ENERGY STAR eligibility requirements, and new construction pre-approval process. Submit with completed W-9 and invoices.

forms.program_name: Wattsmart Business – Oil and Gas Incentives (2025)
forms.form_name: Oil and Gas Incentive Application Package (General Application + Supplement)
forms.form_notes: Three-part package: (1) General Application, (2) Oil & Gas Application Supplement, (3) IRS Form W-9. Must be submitted before pre-inspection. Additional proof of Rocky Mountain Power service may be required for projects in field areas near other service providers.

forms.form_name: Wattsmart Business New Construction / Major Renovation Pre-Approval Application
forms.form_notes: Pre-approval required before construction completion. Submit online application or signed General Application plus IRS Form W-9. Projects completed without pre-authorization are ineligible. Contact Wattsmart Business Trade Ally or Rocky Mountain Power directly to initiate.

forms.provider_name: Cheyenne Light, Fuel and Power (d/b/a Black Hills Energy)
forms.program_name: Commercial and Industrial Demand Side Management (DSM) Electric Rebate Program (2025)
forms.form_notes: Printable application downloadable from the Black Hills Energy program page. Program currently suspended (as of January 1, 2026) pending PSC approval of new DSM plan. Applications were accepted through January 31, 2026 for 2025 installations only.
Application available on LVE rebate program page. Rebate amounts for commercial lighting vary based on kWh savings. Contact LVE at 1-800-882-5875 for current application form and program details.
